newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair orders tough look at public spending.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair orders tough look at public spending.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair and Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown ordered their cabinet colleagues on Thursday to take a hard look at their departmental budgets to make sure money was being well spent, officials said.

One said that Blair and Brown, at the weekly cabinet meeting, told other ministers "in pretty strong terms" of the importance of sticking to agreed spending totals and to find savings where they could.
Ministers were not given a deadline for completing their spending reviews but there was an "expectation of a fairly rigorous approach" to justifying existing programmes, the official said.
If possible savings are identified, ministers would have to make a case for redirecting expenditure within their departments to Chief Secretary to the Treasury Alistair Darling, he added.
Labour has adopted the previous Conservative government's overall spending allocations for this financial year and next.

Brown said in the election campaign that ministers would be expected to use their first year in office to reorder spending, within already announced departmental budgets, to meet Labour's priorities in the 1998-99 financial year.
